issues.legal_issue: A co-owner’s possession through a lessee may become adverse to another co-owner when the lease expressly asserts the lessee’s lessor’s exclusive title and excludes the other co-owner.
material_facts: The father and his minor son were co-owners of the land.
Acting as the minor’s guardian, the father leased the entire property to a relative and expressly asserted the minor’s exclusive title, denying his own co-ownership.
The relative possessed the property as lessee, and the father accepted rent and pursued rent-related proceedings on the minor’s behalf.
The father knew of the circumstances and did not receive rent or otherwise participate in the property’s enjoyment for the statutory period.
issues.conclusion: The minor’s possession through the lessee was adverse to the father from the commencement of the lease, and it continued for the statutory period, giving the minor title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: A co-owner’s possession is ordinarily presumed to be on behalf of all co-owners unless actual ouster is proved. Ouster may be shown by an open assertion of exclusive ownership that denies the other co-owner’s rights. A co-owner’s consent to another’s exclusive possession does not prevent that possession from being adverse, and a lessee’s possession is in law the possession of the lessor. No earlier cases were cited for this principle.

rule.if: coownership_title_proceeding and guardian_leases_property_for_minor and lease_asserts_minor_exclusive_title and other_coowner_knows_of_exclusion and lessee_possession_continues_for_limitation_period

predicates.coownership_title_proceeding: The proceeding concerns competing title claims between co-owners of property.
predicates.guardian_leases_property_for_minor: A guardian leases the property on behalf of a minor co-owner.
predicates.lease_asserts_minor_exclusive_title: The lease asserts the minor’s exclusive title and denies the other co-owner’s interest.
predicates.other_coowner_knows_of_exclusion: The other co-owner knows that the property is being possessed exclusively on the minor’s behalf.
predicates.lessee_possession_continues_for_limitati: The lessee’s possession on behalf of the minor continues for the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When co-owners dispute title and a guardian leases property for a minor while asserting the minor’s exclusive title, the other co-owner knows of the exclusion, and the lessee’s possession continues for the limitation period, the minor acquires title by adverse possession.

issues.legal_issue: A dispossessed co-owner’s later assertion of joint title does not interrupt established adverse possession unless possession changes or the possessing co-owner acknowledges the other’s title or ends the exclusive possession.
material_facts: The father’s earlier acts as guardian had placed the property in the lessee’s possession on behalf of the minor, excluding the father.
The father later executed a mortgage in his personal capacity, asserting his own interest as co-owner.
The property remained in the lessee’s possession, and the father did not re-enter or resume possession.
The minor did not acknowledge the father’s title or discontinue exclusive possession.
issues.conclusion: The father’s later assertion of joint title did not interrupt the minor’s adverse possession; the High Court’s contrary conclusion could not be sustained.
issues.legal_principle: Once a co-sharer’s possession has become adverse by ouster, a mere assertion of joint title by the dispossessed co-sharer does not stop the running of adverse possession. Interruption requires effective re-entry or resumption of possession, acknowledgment of the dispossessed co-owner’s title by the possessor, or discontinuance of exclusive possession. A mental change or assertion unaccompanied by a change in possession is insufficient. No earlier cases were cited for this principle.

rule.if: coowner_adverse_possession_dispute and adverse_possession_already_established and dispossessed_coowner_makes_later_title_assertion and no_effective_reentry and possessor_does_not_acknowledge_title and exclusive_possession_continues

predicates.coowner_adverse_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns adverse possession claimed by one co-owner against another.
predicates.adverse_possession_already_established: The possessing co-owner has already excluded the other co-owner and begun adverse possession.
predicates.dispossessed_coowner_makes_later_title_a: The dispossessed co-owner later asserts a right to joint ownership.
predicates.no_effective_reentry: The dispossessed co-owner does not re-enter or otherwise effectively resume possession.
predicates.possessor_does_not_acknowledge_title: The possessing co-owner does not acknowledge the dispossessed co-owner’s title.
predicates.exclusive_possession_continues: The possessing co-owner’s exclusive possession continues.

issues.definition: Where adverse possession between co-owners is already established, a later title assertion does not interrupt it if there is no effective re-entry, no acknowledgment of the dispossessed co-owner’s title, and exclusive possession continues.
